description: The benign scenario -- a 200 with a well-formed OpenAI-compatible answer. PINS: that the test provider's canned wire response reaches each twin's REAL response mapping and comes back out as the canned text, unchanged, on both sides (Rust llm::map_chat_http_response, Kotlin KlarvoApi.mapCleanupResponse). DOES NOT PIN: any network call (none happens), the request body (the test provider builds none), token accounting beyond 'usage is accepted', or what a real provider would answer.

A 200 whose choice carries an EMPTY content string -- a provider refusal or degenerate completion. This is the reproduction for drift row D2 / D-H19, and story 13-2 CLOSED it. PINS: both twins now reject the answer. Rust raises LlmError::ResponseFormat("Empty content in response"); Kotlin raises KlarvoApi.CleanupResponseFormatException, an IOException that KlarvoOverlayService.isRetryableCleanupFailure names NON-retryable by type -- it carries no "HTTP nnn", so the status regex alone would have read it as a transport failure and burned the provider ladder on a guaranteed repeat. Both are non-retryable: no ladder and no paste; the raw transcript goes to the clipboard with the shipped cleanup-failure cause, and -- as on Desktop -- a history row IS still written carrying that raw transcript. What can no longer be written is a row carrying the empty ANSWER, which is what ADR-0016 row D2 asks for (kein „"-History-Eintrag). Before 13-2 Kotlin returned "", which was pasted into the focused field and stored in history.db as the dictation. Both twins decide AFTER trimming (Kotlin also after sanitizeLlmOutput), so a whitespace-only answer is rejected on both sides -- pinned by llm::tests::spec_whitespace_only_answer_is_rejected_like_an_empty_one and TestProviderScenarioTest.whitespaceOnlyAnswerIsRejectedLikeAnEmptyOne. A control-character-only answer is still asymmetric (Kotlin sanitizes before the check, Rust sanitizes downstream); that residual is recorded in the story, not pinned here. DOES NOT PIN: the wording of either message beyond the substrings asserted here, or the terminal UI state (KlarvoOverlayService.decideDelivery owns that).

A 200 whose choice carries finish_reason == "length" -- the max_tokens cap was hit mid-sentence. Reproduction for drift row D3 / D-M16, CLOSED by story 13-2. PINS: both twins reject it before the content is read. Rust raises LlmError::OutputTruncated; Kotlin raises KlarvoApi.CleanupOutputTruncatedException, non-retryable by type for the same reason as the empty case (a repeat produces the same cap). Before 13-2 Kotlin never inspected finish_reason and pasted the half sentence. DOES NOT PIN: the max_tokens value itself (TWIN-LLM-MAX-TOKENS-001 in twin-constants-vectors.json), or how often the cap is reached in practice.

wire.body: {"choices":[{"message":{"content":"Debug provider canned answer that was cut"},"finish_reason":"length"}]}

description: A 200 carrying a body that genuinely does NOT deserialize: a JSON envelope that ends mid-string, the shape a cut-off or proxy-garbled provider answer has. This is the reproduction for drift row D10 / D-M2, and it reproduces the MECHANISM, not a look-alike. PINS: both halves of that row. Rust -- reqwest's response.json() fails to decode, the error #[from]-converts to LlmError::Request, pipeline::is_retryable_llm_error says TRUE and the production fallback ladder fires (D-M2's Desktop column). Kotlin -- JSONObject(body) still throws a bare org.json.JSONException (the honest outcome for a body that does not parse), but story 13-2 CLOSED the behavioural half: the ladder gate moved into the pure KlarvoOverlayService.isRetryableCleanupFailure, which classifies a JSONException as RETRYABLE, so the single-call path now fires the ladder exactly as the chunked path always did. Before 13-2 the gate read `e is IOException &&` first, JSONException is not one, and a dictation under CHUNK_THRESHOLD degraded straight to clipboard-only. On the CHUNKED path (text >= CHUNK_THRESHOLD 400 bytes) KlarvoApi.collectChunkResults rewraps the same JSONException into an IOException whose message carries no "HTTP nnn", so isRetryableCleanupFailure finds no status and the ladder DOES fire there. The body deliberately contains no "HTTP nnn" substring, so that regex cannot match by accident. The `rust.message_contains` string "error decoding response body" is reqwest 0.12.28's own `Display` text for a decode error (`src/error.rs`, `Kind::Decode`), not a Klarvo string: a reqwest bump may change it, and the load-bearing claims are `rust.error == "Request"` and `rust.retryable == true`, which are pinned separately. DOES NOT PIN: the fallback ladder's membership (Groq is never a cleanup fallback, Epic 12 FR2; `test` is never a candidate either), whether the fallback call succeeds, the exact reqwest/org.json error wording beyond the substring asserted here, or the STT side -- STT parses with serde_json::from_slice and is NON-retryable for the same class of body (see TEST-STT-MALFORMED-001).
expected_divergence: Story 13-2 closed the behavioural half of D10 / D-M2: both platforms now treat an undecodable body as retryable and fire the provider ladder, on the chunked AND the single-call path. What remains is a representation difference that cannot be removed -- Rust surfaces it as LlmError::Request (reqwest's decode error), Kotlin as org.json.JSONException -- and the two twins parse with different libraries by construction. The VERDICT is what is pinned.

description: A 429 with an OpenAI-shaped error body. PINS: both twins map it to their retryable-failure shape -- Rust LlmError::ApiError { status: 429 } (pipeline::is_retryable_llm_error -> true), Kotlin an IOException whose message carries the literal "HTTP 429" that KlarvoOverlayService.isRetryableCleanupFailure regex-matches. Running this scenario end to end therefore fires the PRODUCTION fallback ladder (deepseek -> openai -> openrouter) and makes a real call to the user's configured fallback provider -- intended, and the point of the scenario. DOES NOT PIN: the ladder's membership (Groq is never a cleanup fallback, Epic 12 FR2; `test` is never a candidate either), nor that the fallback call succeeds.

A 503 with an OpenAI-shaped error body -- the server-outage shape. PINS: the same contract as TEST-LLM-HTTP429-001 with a >= 500 status -- Rust LlmError::ApiError { status: 503 } (retryable), Kotlin an IOException carrying the literal "HTTP 503"; the production fallback ladder fires on both. DOES NOT PIN: any other 5xx code, or provider-specific retry-after handling (neither twin reads it).

No response at all: the provider performs a REAL request to http://127.0.0.1:1/ (the loopback discard port), which cannot connect. PINS: a genuine transport error is produced through the real client on both twins -- Rust LlmError::Request (is_retryable_llm_error -> true), Kotlin an IOException whose message carries NO "HTTP nnn", so isRetryableCleanupFailure's regex finds no status and returns true. A synthetic transport error is impossible: reqwest::Error has no public constructor, and a new LlmError variant would touch every match over the enum plus both is_retryable_* predicates. Loopback only -- no byte leaves the device. DOES NOT PIN: the exact OS error text ("Connection refused" is platform-wording), the timeout behaviour, or that port 1 is free (nothing may bind it without root).

STT benign scenario -- a 200 verbose_json body with a transcript and no segments, which extract_verbose_text falls back to. PINS: the canned body reaches the real Rust mapping (stt::map_transcription_http_response) and returns the canned transcript. The Kotlin column is n/a BY CONSTRUCTION, not by oversight: ADR-0017 makes the STT request and its guards shared Rust core, consumed on Android through GroqSttBridge.nativeTranscribe, so there is no Kotlin STT mapping to assert against. DOES NOT PIN: the segment-confidence filter (its own tests live in stt/mod.rs), the JNI sentinel encoding, or Android runtime behaviour.

kotlin.note: STT is shared Rust core (ADR-0017); Android consumes this same provider over JNI.

description: A 200 whose transcript is empty -- the reproduction for drift row D9 / D-M5 (STT returns empty / unparseable text), CLOSED by story 13-2. PINS: Rust maps it to SttError::ResponseFormat, which pipeline::is_retryable_stt_error treats as NON-retryable; on Android the same error now crosses the JNI as its own sentinel `__ERROR_FORMAT:<msg>__` (stt/groq_jni.rs, matched BEFORE the __ERROR_NETWORK: catch-all) and KlarvoOverlayService.classifySttSentinel returns NON_RETRYABLE for it. Before 13-2 it fell into the catch-all and Android burned three Groq calls and ~7 s of backoff on a guaranteed repeat. Also closed here: D-M6, the retry BUDGET -- transcribeWithRetry's retryDelaysMs is empty, so Android makes one attempt like Desktop instead of three. DOES NOT PIN: the local-Whisper safety net or the pending-WAV terminal path (both unchanged, and the "failed after retries" message that gates the net still fires for a retryable exhaustion). NOTE for the reproduction: pipeline::try_local_whisper_fallback can silently rescue a test STT failure on a machine that has a local model downloaded -- remove or rename the model to observe the terminal path.

rust.message_contains: API returned empty text after segment confidence filter

kotlin.note: STT is shared Rust core (ADR-0017). The Kotlin side owns only the sentinel->verdict mapping and the retry budget, both pinned by SttSentinelClassificationTest against the sentinel strings stt/groq_jni.rs emits.

description: A 200 whose body deserializes as NEITHER the verbose_json nor the plain json shape. PINS: Rust reports SttError::ResponseFormat, which pipeline::is_retryable_stt_error treats as NON-retryable -- so unlike the LLM twin's malformed row (TEST-LLM-MALFORMED-001, retryable LlmError::Request) an undecodable STT body does NOT fire a retry. The asymmetry is real, pre-existing and pinned here rather than normalised away: the live STT path reads bytes() and parses with serde_json::from_slice, so the decode failure is caught by our own code and named ResponseFormat, whereas the live LLM path calls response.json() and lets reqwest raise a decode error that maps to the retryable Request variant. The extracted map_transcription_http_response carries that sequence verbatim, so the test provider reports what the real path reports. DOES NOT PIN: the exact serde error text (it is appended to the message and varies by serde version), nor any opinion on which twin is right -- story 13-2 owns the verdict.

A 429 with an OpenAI-shaped error body. PINS: Rust SttError::ApiError { status: 429 }, which is_retryable_stt_error treats as retryable -- the shape D9's retry-budget half needs to be observable on device. On Android the same error arrives as the __ERROR_API:HTTP 429 sentinel that transcribeWithRetry already classifies. DOES NOT PIN: Android's 429-vs-5xx classification gap (audit D-M7), which lives in Kotlin and is out of this story's scope.

A 503 with an OpenAI-shaped error body -- the server-outage shape. PINS: the same contract as TEST-STT-HTTP429-001 with a >= 500 status -- Rust SttError::ApiError { status: 503 }, which is_retryable_stt_error treats as retryable. DOES NOT PIN: any other 5xx code.

No response at all: a REAL request to http://127.0.0.1:1/ which cannot connect. PINS: Rust SttError::Request (retryable), produced through the real reqwest client rather than synthesised. Loopback only -- no byte leaves the device. DOES NOT PIN: the exact OS error text or the timeout behaviour.

An EXPECTED-ABSENCE vector, not a behaviour vector: `truncated` is deliberately NOT offered on the STT side, because SttError carries no truncation variant and there is nothing for a truncated transcript to map to. PINS: the STT scenario picker offers the LLM set MINUS this one, and stt::test_stt_canned_wire resolves the string like `ok` (fail-soft) rather than inventing an outcome. DOES NOT PIN: any user-visible behaviour -- the value is unreachable through the UI.

The option list of the `Test provider (LLM)` row in Settings -> Advanced -> System (expert mode only), story 13-1b. PINS: the row offers exactly the values config::VALID_TEST_PROVIDER_LLM accepts, in that order, `off` first -- read by a Rust test against the constant AND by the desktop proxy harness against the rendered DOM, so the React list cannot drift from the allowlist unnoticed. `off` is IN the list on purpose: the value IS the state, so folding `off` into the scenario set is what makes "provider on but scenario unsaved" impossible to express, and what lets the row switch BACK off without a second control. DOES NOT PIN: the NORMAL provider picker (RecordingAudioContent, SettingsPanel), which must never offer a test-provider value; nor `llmProvider` itself, which this row never writes -- the real provider stays configured while the test provider is on.

kotlin.note: The React settings bundle is the only settings surface on Android (MainActivity : TauriActivity), so there is no Kotlin option list to assert against. Kotlin reads the chosen value back out of config.json via KlarvoApi.parseTestProvider.

description: The option list of the `Test provider (STT)` row in Settings -> Advanced -> System (expert mode only), story 13-1b. PINS: the row offers exactly the values config::VALID_TEST_PROVIDER_STT accepts, in that order -- the LLM set MINUS `truncated`, because SttError has no truncation variant and there would be nothing for a truncated STT answer to map to. Read by a Rust test against the constant AND by the desktop proxy harness against the rendered DOM. DOES NOT PIN: the normal STT picker in RecordingAudioContent (CLOUD_STT_MODELS), which must never offer a test-provider value; nor whether `local` should be hidden on Android -- that gate is story 13-3's.

kotlin.note: STT is shared Rust core (ADR-0017); the row writes advanced.testProviderStt, which Kotlin carries through to the JNI uninspected.
